notes: TGClient -request:completion: routes every reply through -handleUpdate: which runs inside dispatch_async(dispatch_get_main_queue()) (TGClient.m:102) and only ever hands over an NSDictionary (TGClient.m:97). That rules out the off-main-thread and non-dictionary-reply classes of bug for every completion block in this area, and rules out the __block counter races in -searchChatList:completion: (ChatList.m:632) and -titlesForChatIds:completion: (ChatList.m:912).

No 32-bit id truncation found: every chat/user/message id in these five files goes through longLongValue or @(int64_t). The only integerValue uses are on int32 TDLib fields (total_count, dates, folder ids, mute_for, slow_mode_delay).
All request payloads were checked field-by-field against tdlib/td/td/generate/scheme/td_api.tl; no misnamed or missing required scalar fields were found beyond the ones reported below.
No selector collisions between the five TGClient categories, and no method declared in a header without an implementation.

findings.what: -reportNotSpamMessages:inChat:completion: sends the TDLib method that does the exact opposite of what the header promises: `[self cm_toggleSupergroup:@"reportSupergroupSpam" chat:chatId fields:@{@"message_ids" : messageIds ?: @[]} completion:completion];`
findings.failure: TGClient+ChatManagement.h:160 documents this as "Tell the server a message the anti-spam filter removed was not spam." td_api.tl:15025 defines `reportSupergroupSpam supergroup_id:int53 message_ids:vector<int53> = Ok;` - it reports the listed messages AS spam. A user who taps a 'not spam' affordance would report the innocent messages as spam to Telegram, and the call returns ok:YES so the UI confirms success. The method has no callers today, so this is a live trap for the next screen that wires it up rather than a bug the user can hit right now.
findings.fix: Either delete the method, or change the TDLib method name to @"reportSupergroupAntiSpamFalsePositive" and the field to a single @"message_id" (td_api.tl requires `reportSupergroupAntiSpamFalsePositive supergroup_id:int53 message_id:int53`) - which is exactly what -reportAntiSpamFalsePositiveForMessage:inChat:completion: at line 468 already does, so deleting -reportNotSpamMessages:inChat:completion: from both the .h and .m is the correct fix.

findings.what: -markForumTopicReadInChat:topic:completion: only sends readAllForumTopicMentions, readAllForumTopicReactions and readAllForumTopicPollVotes; it never marks the topic's messages read (no viewMessages / force_read).
findings.failure: TGTopicsViewController.m:1197 wires this to the row action whose key is "read" and whose failure text is "Could not mark the topic as read."; TGTopicsViewController.m:1037 also calls it when a topic is opened. A topic with 12 unread ordinary messages and no mentions keeps its unread badge: all three requests answer ok, the completion reports success, -reloadTopics re-fetches getForumTopics and the same unread_count:12 comes back. Tapping 'Mark as read' repeatedly never clears the badge.
findings.fix: After the three existing requests, chain a getForumTopic (chat_id, forum_topic_id) and, when the reply's last_message.id is non-zero, send `@{@"@type":@"viewMessages", @"chat_id":@(chatId), @"message_ids":@[lastMessageId], @"source":@{@"@type":@"messageSourceForumTopicHistory"}, @"force_read":@YES}` (messageSourceForumTopicHistory exists at td_api.tl:3186), then call completion. -markChatAsRead:completion: in TGClient+ChatList.m:785 is the working template for this.

findings.what: TGCMEventFilterFields() lists only 13 of the 15 chatEventLogFilters booleans - `member_tag_changes` and `subscription_extensions` are missing from the map, and -eventLogForChat: builds the filter object from that map alone (line 1047: `for (NSString *key in fields) filter[fields[key]] = @(!filters || [filters containsObject:key]);`).
findings.failure: td_api.tl:7854 declares `chatEventLogFilters ... member_tag_changes:Bool ... subscription_extensions:Bool`. Every field the JSON omits is parsed as false, so the two omitted filters are always off - including on the 'All actions' path where `filters` is nil and the code intends every flag to be YES. Concretely: an admin changes another admin's custom title (a member_tag_change) and TGChatEventsViewController's Recent Actions list never shows that row, with no way for the user to turn it on.
findings.fix: Add `@"memberTagChanges" : @"member_tag_changes"` and `@"subscriptionExtensions" : @"subscription_extensions"` to TGCMEventFilterFields() at line 99, and document the two new filter keys in the -eventLogForChat: comment in TGClient+ChatManagement.h so the filter picker in TGChatEventsViewController can offer them.

findings.what: -myRightsInChat:completion: reads a field that does not exist in this TDLib schema: `NSString *title = TGCMString(status[@"custom_title"]);` where `status` is a ChatMemberStatus object.
findings.failure: td_api.tl:2475-2492 defines chatMemberStatusCreator/Administrator/Member/Restricted with no custom_title member at all - this schema carries the title on `chatMember.tag` (td_api.tl:2508) instead. TGCMString of a missing key returns @"", so the "customTitle" key the header promises at TGClient+ChatManagement.h:77 is permanently the empty string for owners and admins alike. Any screen that renders it shows nothing where the group owner's title ("Founder", etc.) should appear.
findings.fix: Either drop "customTitle" from -myRightsInChat: and from its header contract at TGClient+ChatManagement.h:77, or populate it correctly: chain a getChatMember reply's `tag` field (TGCMString(result[@"tag"]) at line 533, not status[@"custom_title"]). TGClient+Groups.m:159 already reads `member[@"tag"]` and is the correct version.

findings.what: -setSlowModeDelay:forChat: snaps downward, not to the nearest preset: `for (NSNumber *preset in [TGClient slowModePresets]) { if ([preset integerValue] <= seconds) allowed = [preset integerValue]; }`
findings.failure: TGClient+ChatManagement.h:120 says the value is rounded to "the nearest allowed value". With presets @[0,10,30,60,300,900,3600], a caller asking for 800 seconds gets 300 (nearest is 900), 250 gets 60 (nearest is 300), and anything under 10 silently disables slow mode entirely. A caller that computes a delay rather than picking from -slowModePresets sets a far weaker restriction than requested and gets ok:YES.
findings.fix: Replace the loop with a nearest-value search: track the preset minimising llabs(preset - seconds), breaking ties toward the larger preset; or change the header text at TGClient+ChatManagement.h:120 to say the value is rounded down to the next allowed preset.

findings.what: TGClient+Groups.m (1447 lines) is a second, largely unused implementation of TGClient+ChatManagement.m (1107 lines). Both categories implement the same TDLib calls with different helper names (TGDict/TGArray/TGString/TGIsError vs TGCMDict/TGCMArray/TGCMString/TGCMFailed; TGPermissionKeys vs TGCMPermissionFields; TGAdminRightKeys vs TGCMRightFields; tg_group: vs cm_supergroupForChat:; tg_supergroupToggle: vs cm_toggleSupergroup:; tg_link: vs cm_requestLink:; TGFlattenInviteLink vs TGCMFlatInviteLink) and different output key vocabularies (snake_case TDLib names in Groups, camelCase in ChatManagement).
findings.failure: 40 of TGClient+Groups.h's public methods have no caller anywhere in src/ - the entire invite-link stack (primaryInviteLinkForGroup:, replacePrimaryInviteLinkForGroup:, createInviteLinkInGroup:..., inviteLinksInGroup:..., inviteLinkCountsInGroup:), the entire join-request stack (joinRequestsInGroup:limit:, processAllJoinRequestsInGroup:), all of createBasicGroupWithTitle:/createSupergroupWithTitle:/upgradeBasicGroupToSupergroup:, setGroupChat:title:/description:/photoAtPath:/username:, every setGroup:* switch, eventLogForGroup:, reportGroup:, suitableDiscussionGroupsWithCompletion:, createdPublicChatsWithCompletion:. TGInviteLinksViewController uses the ChatManagement versions exclusively. The cost is ~700 lines of armv7 code and its literal dictionaries resident in a 512MB device, plus the standing hazard that the two key vocabularies get crossed: a dictionary from -defaultPermissionsInGroup: (keys "can_send_basic_messages", ...) passed to -setPermissions:forChat: (reads keys "sendMessages", ...) would send an all-false chatPermissions and silently mute the whole group.
findings.fix: Delete from TGClient+Groups.{h,m} the 40 unreferenced methods listed by the caller scan, and with them the now-orphaned TGFlattenInviteLink and tg_link:completion: helpers. Keep the 20 methods TGGroupMembersViewController/TGProfileViewController actually call (groupInfoForChat:, membersInGroup:..., searchMembersInGroup:..., memberStatusOfUser:..., administratorRightsOfUser:..., permissionsOfUser:..., myAdministratorRightsInGroup:, defaultPermissionsInGroup:, promoteMember:..., restrictMember:..., banMember:..., removeMember:..., unbanMember:..., deleteAllMessagesFromUser:..., administratorRightKeys, memberPermissionKeys, titleFor*Key:). Do not merge the two key vocabularies in the same pass - each surviving method's callers depend on its current spelling.

findings.what: -setOnFoldersChanged: copies its block into a file-static that is never cleared: `static void (^TGFoldersChangedBlock)(void) = nil;` (line 68) / `TGFoldersChangedBlock = [block copy];` (line 932). Neither -setOnFoldersChanged: nor its getter -onFoldersChanged has a caller anywhere in src/.
findings.failure: Dead today; a leak the moment it is used. A view controller calling `[client setOnFoldersChanged:^{ [self reload]; }]` captures self strongly into a process-lifetime static, so the controller and its whole view hierarchy are never deallocated even after being popped - on a 40-60MB budget that is a permanent tens-of-KB-per-visit leak. TGFoldersViewController.m:137 already uses the NSNotificationCenter path (TGChatFoldersDidChangeNotification), which is the correct one.
findings.fix: Delete -setOnFoldersChanged:, -onFoldersChanged, the TGFoldersChangedBlock static (line 68) and its invocation at line 97-98 from TGClient+ChatList.m, plus their declarations in TGClient+ChatList.h. -beginObservingFolderChanges and the notification stay.

findings.what: -joinGroupByInviteLink:completion: branches on a result type this schema never produces and silently swallows two it does: `else if ([type isEqualToString:@"chat"]) completion([result[@"id"] longLongValue], NO); else completion(0, NO);`
findings.failure: td_api.tl:13965 declares `joinChatByInviteLink invite_link:string = ChatJoinResult;` with exactly four cases (chatJoinResultSuccess, chatJoinResultRequestSent, chatJoinResultGuardBotApprovalRequired, chatJoinResultDeclined). The @"chat" branch is unreachable dead code left over from an older schema, while chatJoinResultDeclined and chatJoinResultGuardBotApprovalRequired both fall into the final `completion(0, NO)`, which is byte-identical to a network error. A user whose join was declined by the group's guard bot gets the generic failure message instead of the real reason. The same shape exists in TGClient+ChatManagement.m:867-872 (which has no chatJoinResultSuccess branch at all and instead reads result[@"chat_id"] unconditionally, giving 0 for the two unhandled cases).
findings.fix: In TGClient+Groups.m:1145-1153 delete the @"chat" branch and add explicit handling: on @"chatJoinResultDeclined" and @"chatJoinResultGuardBotApprovalRequired" the completion needs a way to say 'refused, not failed' - widen the completion to (int64_t chatId, BOOL requestSent, NSString *refusal) or add a third state, and mirror the same four-case switch in TGClient+ChatManagement.m:867.

findings.what: -setGroup:slowModeDelay:completion: forwards the caller's seconds straight through with no validation: `@"slow_mode_delay" : @(seconds)`, unlike -setSlowModeDelay:forChat: in TGClient+ChatManagement.m:385 which snaps to a preset.
findings.failure: TDLib rejects setChatSlowModeDelay for any value outside {0,10,30,60,300,900,3600} with an error, so this method answers NO for e.g. 45 seconds while the ChatManagement twin answers YES having quietly applied 30. Two APIs on the same class disagree about the contract for the same TDLib call. Currently dead (no callers), so the disagreement is latent.
findings.fix: Delete -setGroup:slowModeDelay:completion: as part of the TGClient+Groups dead-code removal above; -setSlowModeDelay:forChat:completion: is the surviving API.

findings.what: TGChatTitleCache() is a process-lifetime NSMutableDictionary with no eviction, written on every chat-list render: `if ([row[@"title"] isKindOfClass:NSString.class] && [row[@"title"] length] > 0) TGChatTitleCache()[chatId] = row[@"title"];` inside -tgcl_rowsForChatIds:, plus writes at lines 858 and 890. TGMarkedUnreadChatIds() (line 54) is the same pattern.
findings.failure: Every chat id the user ever scrolls past, searches for, or gets a title lookup on keeps an NSNumber key and an NSString title alive until the process dies; searchPublicChats results count too, so global search over many queries grows it without bound. On the 4S's ~40-60MB budget this is tens of KB after heavy use rather than a crash, but it is unbounded and it duplicates data self.chatsById already holds (the cache exists only to survive chatsById evictions).
findings.fix: Cap it: in -tgcl_rowsForChatIds: skip the cache write when self.chatsById already holds the title (it always does at that point - the row came from chatsById), which removes the search-result growth entirely; or replace both statics with an NSCache with countLimit 200 and drop them in -didReceiveMemoryWarning / -logOut.
